title: Metric explorer
description: Requirement 7. One panel per metric, generated from the $metric variable's repeat rather than one panel per metric hand-built in this JSON. The variable is scoped to metrics that currently have at least one observation: a metric.metric_key with no data yet is a data-source gap, not something a panel should render as a permanently empty tile (see CLAUDE.md, 'a flat or empty panel is a data-source bug'). Add a row to metric and start sending it data, and a panel appears here with no dashboard edit. The query uses IN ($metric), not = '$metric': $metric is multi-valued, so Grafana quotes each value itself and wrapping it again produces ''value''. This dashboard deliberately spans every capture epoch, so individual series are sparse; the per-dataset dashboards show each capture at its own scale.

list.name: metric
list.label: Metric
list.query: SELECT metric_key FROM metric WHERE metric_key IN (SELECT DISTINCT metric_key FROM observation) ORDER BY metric_key;

targets.rawSql:
SELECT $__timeGroup(event_time, '$__interval') AS time, avg(value_raw) AS "raw", avg(value) AS "calibrated"
FROM observation
WHERE metric_key IN ($metric) AND $__timeFilter(event_time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;
